claims.claim: Alkalinity and ANC are determined by identical electrometric acidimetric titration procedures; the only difference is that the alkalinity sample is filtered and the ANC sample is not.

claims.claim: Alkalinity is the acid neutralizing capacity of solutes in a water sample, consisting of the sum of titratable carbonate and noncarbonate chemical species in a filtered sample.

claims.claim: ANC is the acid-neutralizing capacity of solutes plus particulates in an unfiltered water sample and is equivalent to alkalinity for samples without titratable particulate matter.

ANC is equivalent to

gaps: Alkalinity and ANC are not among the six metrics this system measures, and the document gives no way to infer alkalinity or ANC from any sonde-measurable parameter. Every value it produces comes from a bench acidimetric titration of a grab sample.

Gives no pH calibration procedure at all. It requires a calibrated pH electrode and meter but refers all calibration, buffer selection, buffer values, slope and offset acceptance criteria, and electrode maintenance to NFM 6.4. An operator asking 'how do I calibrate pH' will retrieve alkalinity chunks that say only 'follow the instructions in NFM 6.4'.

The many pH numbers in this document (8.3 and 4.5 equivalence points, the 4.8-4.3 sensitive region, the 8.1 and 5.5 titration thresholds, the 10.3 Gran cutoff) are titration-curve landmarks, not pH measurement specifications. It states no pH measurement accuracy, resolution, or drift tolerance, so a question about acceptable pH accuracy retrieves plausible-looking numbers that answer a different question.

Gives no temperature measurement procedure or accuracy criterion. It requires a calibrated thermometer but defers selection and calibration criteria entirely to NFM 6.1. Temperature appears here only as reagent storage limits (below 25-30 degrees C), the instruction to equilibrate titrant to sample temperature, the Na2CO3 drying temperature (150-160 degrees C), and the Kelvin conversion in the acid-dissociation-constant equation.

Uses conductivity as a decision threshold in at least four places (Gran method when conductivity is below 100 microsiemens per centimeter, no magnetic stirrer below 100 microsiemens per centimeter, titrate to pH 5.5 below 100 microsiemens per centimeter, deionized water at 1 microsiemen per centimeter maximum) but gives no method for measuring specific conductance: no cell constant, no calibration standard values, no measurement procedure. It defines the unit as microsiemens per centimeter at 25 degrees C without stating the temperature-compensation relationship.

Gives no turbidity content. Turbidity appears once, as a footnote URL to a parameter-code spreadsheet. Particulate matter is handled by 0.45-micrometer filtration, not by measuring or thresholding turbidity, so there is no turbidity value, unit, or interference threshold here.

Dissolved oxygen is never mentioned. The document warns against aeration and against oxidation of hydrogen sulfide, ferrous iron, and manganous manganese during sample handling, and describes anoxic and suboxic sampling by cross-reference, but contains no DO measurement, no saturation values, no air-calibration procedure, and no altitude or salinity correction.

ORP and redox potential are never mentioned as measured quantities. The oxidation and inert-gas cautions are sample-preservation instructions, not redox measurement guidance; there is no Eh, no millivolt reading, no ZoBell's solution, and no reference-electrode offset table.

Gives no continuous or in-situ monitoring guidance. Every procedure is a discrete bench titration. It cites Wagner and others (2006), TM 1-D3, for continuous water-quality monitors but reproduces none of its content, so sensor fouling, drift, field-audit criteria, and record-correction rules are absent.

The quality-control criteria here (duplicate titrations no less than every tenth sample, plus or minus 5 percent reproducibility, plus or minus 10 percent for low alkalinity or high particulate matter) apply to a titration on split aliquots. They are not sensor accuracy or calibration-drift criteria, and cannot answer a question about acceptable drift for a deployed probe.

Gives no relationship between alkalinity and specific conductance and no way to estimate either from the other, despite citing Roberson and others (1963) on differences between field and laboratory determinations of pH, alkalinity, and specific conductance.

Gives no salinity or estuarine correction. It states only that the titration procedures apply to 'fresh to saline' samples, with no ionic-strength correction procedure; activity corrections are declared out of scope and pushed to PHREEQC or the Alkalinity Calculator.

Gives no field-measurable interference thresholds for the six metrics. Interference guidance is qualitative (note color, odor, or previous chemical analysis) or defined by alkalinity magnitude, never by a measured DO, ORP, conductivity, or turbidity value.

Tables arrive as tab-separated bare numbers with their column headers stacked as separate lines (Tables 6.6-1, 6.6-2, 6.6-3, 6.6-7). All figure content (figures 6.6-1 through 6.6-7) is lost; only captions and axis tick values survive, so the summary flowchart of titration procedures in figure 6.6-1 is unavailable. The corpus quality filter removed intervening chunks: content jumps from page 24 at chunk 18 to page 28 at chunk 19, so Example IPT-2's narrative and Tables 6.6-4 and 6.6-5 are absent, and chunks 19 and 25 open with orphaned rows of titration data whose headers no longer exist in the corpus. Internal inconsistency: Table 6.6-1 (chunk 3) lists a 25-mL buret with 0.05-mL graduations and a 10-mL buret with 0.02-mL graduations, while section 6.6.4.A 'Buret titrator' (chunk 15) specifies a 10-mL semimicroburet with 0.05-mL graduations and a 25-mL buret with 0.1-mL graduations. The 400-character overlap duplicates several rules across consecutive chunks (minimum three digital counts, Gran titration to pH 3.5 or lower, the F1-followed-by-F2 note); each is attributed to the chunk where it originates. Chunks 34 and 35 are pure reference list and acknowledgments and carry no extractable claim.
